subject.name_or_desc: A friend of a London merchant asked on the merchant's behalf

context.question: What think you of the ship — is she sunk, or living? And afterwards: where is she, on what coast, and when will news come of her?
context.setting: December 1644: the merchant had sent a ship to trade to the coast of Spain; repeated news said she was wrecked; insurers refused to insure her at £60 per cent or on any terms

attachments.ascendant: Cancer (the ascending degrees of Cancer shew the bulk/body of the ship)
attachments.key_positions: Saturn in Aries in the 11th casting a square very near the Ascendant; Moon, lady of the Ascendant, in Taurus in the 11th in her exaltation, applying by trine to Sun and Mercury in the 7th (wanting but a few minutes of a perfect trine) and near the body of Jupiter; South Node (Cauda) in the 9th; Part of Fortune disposed of by Mars; Mercury in reception with Mars
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
